sheet-87.description: Sheet 87 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers farmland along County Avenue at the southern end of Secaucus, south of sheets 90 and 91. County Avenue runs down the sheet from the top, slightly to the right, to the fork at the bottom where it divides into New County Road heading to the south east and New County Road heading to the south west, both continuing onto sheet 88. Long narrow farm lots, separated by fence lines, run off both sides of the avenue. The buildings are scattered and mostly small: dwellings, pig houses, cook houses, sheds, a hay storage building and a blacksmith shop along the avenue, with a few larger groups of buildings, including stables and storage sheds, near the fork and on the lots to the west. A cluster of farm buildings stands near the top of the sheet east of the avenue. Much of the east half and the lower west part of the sheet is open ground. Water pipes run along County Avenue and the Jersey City supply main follows New County Road. A north arrow is printed at the upper left and the scale bar at the bottom left; the neighbouring sheet numbers 90, 91 and 88 are printed in the margins.
notes: The fork does not survive: County Avenue now runs on as New County Road to the south west and County Road leaves it about 150 m south of the County Avenue / New County Road node. The fork was taken 69 m south west of that node along County Avenue's line, a position supported by the Erie Railroad lines on sheet 88; uncertain by about 20 m.
Placed from the fork and a derived point on County Avenue (helmert, scale held at 3.886 px/ft); low confidence.
Parcel corners along County Avenue lie 2 to 4 m from the drawn lot lines through this placement.

County Av running down the sheet to its fork with New County Rd at the bottom; farms; 100 ft; sparse, few junctions. Anchored on the old County Av / New County Rd fork (69 m SW of the modern node) plus a derived County Av point; low confidence.

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the meadows south of County Avenue at the southern end of Secaucus, towards Snake Hill. County Avenue enters at the upper right and ends at the fork with New County Road, which runs down the middle of the sheet to the south west and becomes the road to Snake Hill at the bottom. Two lanes run diagonally across the middle of the sheet. Two railroads cross the sheet from side to side: the Erie Railroad near the top, four tracks wide, and below it the Erie Railroad Main Line, marked as under construction. A right of way for a water pipe to the Jersey City reservoirs runs from the upper right. At the bottom of the sheet are the yards of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, with a large round house and turntable, a general storage building, sidings, a station and offices, and the County Building beside the road to Snake Hill. A small Y.M.C.A. building of the Lackawanna railroad stands beside New County Road. The rest of the sheet is open meadow with a few dwellings and sheds, and the edge of a creek shows at the left margin. Sheet 87 adjoins at the top.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point at the old fork of County Avenue and New County Road (taken 69 m south west of the modern County Avenue / New County Road node) with the scale of sheet 90 and a north direction worked out from sheet 87; anchored, low confidence, probably 20 to 40 m off at the bottom of the sheet.
Through this placement the modern rail lines of the Secaucus Junction area run close to and nearly parallel with the drawn Erie Railroad tracks.
The road layout is gone: the area is now Secaucus Junction, the New Jersey Turnpike and the Xchange development.

New County Rd, County Av, Lane, road to Snake Hill; Erie and DL&W (Boonton) railroad lines, roundhouse and County Bldg at the bottom; 100 ft; marsh. Anchored on the same fork with north -61 (from sheet 87's drawn County Av); no rail crossing detected; low confidence, 20-40 m possible at the bottom.

sheet-89.description: Sheet 89 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows open meadow on the west side of County Avenue in southern Secaucus, north of sheet 90. Almost the whole sheet is blank marsh. Division Creek runs down the left side from the top. County Avenue runs down the right edge and bends at the fork where Secaucus Avenue leaves it towards the south east; only the start of Secaucus Avenue is drawn, and the rest lies on sheets 95 and 96. A small group of dwellings, sheds and a pig pen stands on the west side of County Avenue just north of the fork, and a few more buildings stand near the top of the sheet along the creek and at the upper right. Across the bottom of the sheet a paper subdivision is drawn: blocks numbered 1 to 11 along the north side of Central Avenue, with 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets running up from it, all set at an angle to the sheet; the same streets continue on sheet 90 below. Only one building stands in the subdivision, near 2nd Street. Water pipes run along County Avenue. The sheet numbers of the neighbours are printed in the margins: 98 at the top, 96 and 95 to the right and 90 at the bottom.
notes: The fork of County Avenue and Secaucus Avenue is not the modern County Avenue / Secaucus Road junction: sheet 90 places it about 400 m further north, near today's UPS Drive; the modern Secaucus Road west end is a later cut.
Placed only from three points of the paper streets along Central Avenue carried from sheet 90 (helmert); the upper part of the sheet is extrapolated and low confidence.
The cut-off label at the fork reads 'SECAU...', the start of Secaucus Avenue.

Mostly blank meadow between Division (Cromakill?) Creek and County Av; paper streets 1st-6th Sts and Central Av at the bottom; 100 ft. Placed from three paper-street points carried from sheet 90 (helmert); the 1910 Secaucus Av fork is not the modern County Av / Secaucus Rd node; low confidence.

sheet-90.description: Sheet 90 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers meadow land on the west side of County Avenue in the southern part of Secaucus, between County Avenue, which runs down the right edge of the sheet, and Division Creek, which winds down the left side. Most of the sheet is a paper subdivision of numbered blocks and narrow lots, marked as not opened: Central Avenue along the top with 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets running down from it, and a second group of blocks across the middle along Washington Avenue, with the numbered streets and Bloomfield and Clinton further down near the creek. Block numbers from 1 to 18 are printed on the blocks. Very little is built: a handful of dwellings and sheds stand along the west side of County Avenue, some near the top of the sheet and others along Kuntz Lane, a short lane running in from County Avenue near the middle right. Across County Avenue only the ends of the side streets on the east side are drawn and named in the margin: a lane near the top, Washington Avenue, Secaucus Avenue (Weigand's Lane), Charles Street and Louis Street; the blocks east of the avenue belong to sheets 95, 92 and 91. Water pipes run along County Avenue. A large part of the lower middle of the sheet, between the subdivision and County Avenue, is open ground. Sheet 89 adjoins at the top and sheet 87 at the bottom.
notes: Secaucus Avenue (Weigands Lane) is Weigands Lane in OpenStreetMap; the modern Secaucus Road meets County Avenue about 180 m further north, on ground the sheet leaves blank, so it is a later road.
The paper streets west of County Avenue (Central Avenue, the numbered streets, Bloomfield, Clinton, Kuntz Lane) do not survive; the area is now industrial (Metro Way, Enterprise Avenue).
Placed from the four junctions of County Avenue with the streets on its east side only (helmert); the subdivision away from County Avenue is placed by extrapolation.

Paper subdivision west of County Av: Central Av, Washington Av, Bloomfield, Clinton, 1st-6th Sts, Kuntz Lane; Division Creek on the left; 100 ft. County Av junctions with Washington Av, Weigands Lane, Charles, Louis detected (helmert, 0.63 m); medium-low confidence away from County Av.

sheet-91.description: Sheet 91 covers a block of open, mostly unbuilt land south of the centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned so that County Avenue crosses the top of the sheet on a slant and the other streets run down the page. The streets are laid out as a paper subdivision: Louis Street and Charles Street run from County Avenue to the foot of the sheet, and Weigand Lane, also lettered as Secaucus Avenue, bounds the blocks on the right. Moller Street and Henry Street cross them at right angles. Almost all of the ground is divided into long narrow lots, numbered along each frontage, and very few of them carry buildings. The built-up parts are a handful of small frame dwellings and sheds in the blocks beside County Avenue, a group of small buildings and a saloon at the upper left, and a cluster of small dwellings and sheds along the left margin near the middle of the sheet, where it adjoins sheet 87. An eight-inch water pipe runs along County Avenue, with a six-inch branch turning south at the top of the sheet. At the foot two lines cross the sheet obliquely: they are a sixty-foot street continued from sheet 94, and the sheet's bottom right corner is cut by a street running south east. The margin names the adjoining sheets: 90 above, 87 to the left, 92 to the right and 94 below. A compass rose stands at the upper right.
notes: Sheet title block reads Hudson Co. Vol. 8A.
Weigand Lane is Weigands Lane in OpenStreetMap, and only its meeting with Moller Street survives; the lane is drawn with only its west side and a boundary line on the right.
Henry Street and the lower part of Louis and Charles Streets are not in the modern street network near this sheet; only Moller Street and the County Avenue junctions were used for control.
The sheet's streets are drawn slightly longer between Louis and Charles Streets than modern parcels allow (about 3 percent); fitted scale 7.78 px/ft against about 7.50 elsewhere in the atlas.
County Av (top), Louis, Charles, Secaucus Av (Weigand Lane), Moller, Henry; 50 ft.

sheet-92.description: Sheet 92 shows the southern edge of the built-up part of Secaucus at 50 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned so that County Avenue crosses the top of the sheet on a slant. Washington Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet from County Avenue, and Weigand's Lane, also lettered Secaucus Avenue, runs down the left margin; at the left edge Moller Street and Henry Street meet it from the adjoining sheet 91. East of Washington Avenue three cross streets are laid out, Garden, Willow and Meadow, enclosing blocks 4 to 6 that are cut into narrow lots but almost entirely empty. The development is at the top and along the west side of Washington Avenue. Near County Avenue stand a blacksmith shop, a wagon house with sheds and several small frame dwellings. The Washington Hook and Ladder Company fire department building, with a bell tower, hose wagon and truck, fronts Washington Avenue below them. West of that, in the open ground between Washington Avenue and Weigand's Lane, a group of greenhouses with glass roofs stands in long narrow ranges, some coloured pink for glass, with a second set of ranges at the upper left. Elsewhere the sheet is blank meadow, drawn only as street lines and lot numbers. Eight-inch and six-inch water pipes run along County Avenue. A compass rose stands at the upper left, and the margin names sheets 90 above, 91 and 94 on the left and below, and 95 to the right and below.
notes: Garden, Willow and Meadow are printed without a suffix and the streets are not in today's street network near this sheet; the Garden Street and Willow Avenue in OpenStreetMap lie elsewhere in Secaucus.
Washington Avenue is drawn much longer than the surviving modern Washington Avenue, which is a short stub south of County Avenue.
Weigand's Lane is Weigands Lane in OpenStreetMap, where it is a short street; the sheet draws it 20 feet wide.

Control rests on three junctions (County Avenue with Washington Avenue and Weigands Lane, and Moller Street with Weigands Lane), so the fit passes exactly through them; fitted scale about 6 percent above the usual 50 ft constant, as the modern streets here are about 4 percent shorter than drawn.
County Av, Weigand's Lane / Secaucus Av, Washington Av, Garden, Willow, Meadow, Moller and Henry Sts at the margin; 50 ft.

sheet-93.description: Sheet 93 shows the marsh-edge district along Penhorn Creek south of the centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Penhorn Avenue runs down the page. A strip of narrow lots, numbered from 194 to 242, lines the east side of Penhorn Avenue along the left margin, and nearly all of it is occupied by pig farms: long pig houses, cook houses, sheds, a barrel storage building, a hay storage shed and a fat rendering works with an engine house at the lower left. Dwellings are few and scattered. A second Penhorn Avenue, with its own row of lot numbers, runs down the right-hand part of the sheet and is lined almost entirely by empty land. Penhorn Creek winds across the sheet between them, with a six-inch water pipe and a dashed track beside it on the west bank, and a heavy straight line, probably a municipal boundary, crosses the sheet and jogs sharply in the middle. At the top left Secaucus Avenue crosses the corner of the sheet beside the Pennsylvania Railroad main line, with a water pipe in the avenue and an unnamed street shown as not named. A 7th Street is drawn marked not open, beside the premises of L. Heflich with pig houses. At the foot, a 10th Street is lettered beside the scale. A compass rose stands in the upper middle. The margin names sheet 94 to the left.
notes: Placed as an anchored part: one junction (Penhorn Avenue and Secaucus Road) estimated from the drawn street edges, north and scale from the config; low confidence.
7th Street is lettered 'Not Open' and another street is lettered 'Not Named'; neither is used for control.

The 'Penhorn Avenue' pair of streets and the creek crossing make the sheet hard to match to the modern network; the identification of the left-hand Penhorn Avenue with the modern one rests on a single junction and on the predicted position of 7th Street.
The sheet number 93 and the sheet 94 label at the left margin were read at full resolution; 10th Street was read at the lower margin and is less certain.
Penhorn Av, Penhorn Creek, Secaucus Av at top left, heavy boundary line (probably the North Bergen / Jersey City line) down the middle; 50 ft.

sheet-94.description: Sheet 94 covers the southern approach to Secaucus at 50 feet to an inch. The main feature is Secaucus Avenue, also lettered Weigand's Lane, which runs from the top of the sheet in a long, nearly straight diagonal to the lower right, where it meets the line of the avenue that continues north east as a wide road, and Penhorn Avenue, which crosses the foot of the sheet with the tracks of a railroad running diagonally through it. Charles Street meets the sheet at the top left, and Washington Avenue at the top right. The land is mostly empty on the west side of the avenue, with a compass rose and a few lot lines. On the east side, between the top of the sheet and the middle, stands a row of pig farms: long pig houses, sheds, cook houses and dwellings, with larger groups of buildings near the middle and a saloon and dwellings and a blacksmith shop near the junction at the foot of the avenue. Water pipes run in the avenue and in Penhorn Avenue. The margin names sheet 91 at the top left, sheet 92 at the top right, sheet 95 at the right and sheet 93 at the foot.
notes: Placed as an anchored part on one junction (Penhorn Avenue and Secaucus Road) whose centre was estimated from the drawn edges; low confidence.
Secaucus Avenue (Weigand's Lane) is today Secaucus Road at its south east end; the section north west of the bend survives only as Weigands Lane near Moller Street.
Rails run in Penhorn Avenue and cross the foot of the sheet; they are not used for control.
Secaucus Av (Weigand's Lane), Secaucus Av, Penhorn Av, railroad at lower left, Charles St and Washington Av at the top; 50 ft.

sheet-95.description: Sheet 95 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers a wide area east of Washington Avenue at the southern edge of Secaucus. County Avenue crosses the top of the sheet on a slant, with a water pipe and the fork of Central Avenue, a paper street from sheet 89, meeting it at the top right. Secaucus Avenue runs from the left margin diagonally across the sheet to the upper right, and a street lettered only Lane, the continuation of Weigand's Lane, comes down from County Avenue to meet it. At the left margin the ends of Garden, Willow and Meadow Streets show where the sheet adjoins sheet 92. Most of the sheet is open ground divided by property lines. Settlement lies along Secaucus Avenue, in two groups: a cluster of small houses, sheds and pig houses at the upper right, and a larger group of houses, sheds, pig farms and dwellings at the lower left, set between the avenue and Penhorn Creek. Penhorn Creek winds across the lower half of the sheet from the right edge to the foot of the sheet, a tidal stream with marsh on both banks. A compass rose stands at the upper left. The margin names sheets 90 and 89 above, 92 and 94 to the left and 96 to the right.
notes: Placed from four points carried from sheet 92 (the edges of Garden and Willow Streets at the shared lot line), with scale and rotation held to sheet 92's; low to medium confidence.
Garden, Willow and Meadow Streets are lettered 'St.' and Central Avenue 'Av.'; none survives near this sheet in today's street network.
The street lettered Lane is Weigand's Lane in sheets 91, 92 and 94; the lettering here is only 'Lane'.
Secaucus Avenue's north east run follows modern Secaucus Road.
County Av, Secaucus Av, Lane, Penhorn Creek, Garden, Willow and Meadow Sts at the left margin; 100 ft.

sheet-96.description: Sheet 96 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers open meadow on the east side of County Avenue in southern Secaucus, between County Avenue and Penhorn Creek. County Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, with the water main along it, and at the lower left reaches the fork where Secaucus Avenue leaves it towards the south east; both roads continue onto sheet 95 below. Penhorn Creek winds down the right half of the sheet from the top to the bottom edge. Between the avenue and the creek the land is almost entirely empty meadow, divided by a few long property lines; only a handful of small buildings are drawn, a dwelling near the top of County Avenue, a few sheds along the avenue, and a small group of dwellings and sheds near the fork on Secaucus Avenue. A dash-dot match line with lettered ends crosses the top of the sheet, marking the edge of sheet 99. The margins name the neighbouring sheets: 98 and 89 to the left, 99 at the top and 95 at the bottom. A north arrow is printed in the upper right part of the sheet and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The fork of County Avenue and Secaucus Avenue does not survive; through sheet 89's placement it falls on modern County Avenue about 70 m north of UPS Drive. Today's Secaucus Road meets County Avenue about 400 m further south.
Placed from the fork and a hydrant beside it, carried from sheet 89, with the scale of sheet 90 and a north direction from the drawn County Avenue (anchored); low confidence.
County Av and its fork with Secaucus Av at the bottom, Penhorn Creek; mostly blank meadow; 100 ft.

sheet-97.description: Sheet 97 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north is toward the upper right. The left half is a paper subdivision of 60 foot streets and narrow lots that was laid out but little built: Bayley, Corrigan, Central and Doane Avenues run across the sheet and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets run down it, with the blocks numbered 1 to 4, 9 to 16 and 19 to 22. The only buildings are a piggery with several sheds in block 11 and a small building in block 14. Central Avenue is also marked as 5th Street where it reaches Post's Lane. East of the subdivision is open farm land crossed by two lanes, a lane running along the top and another running diagonally up to Post's Lane, with long lot lines dividing the ground. A group of piggery buildings, sheds and a small building stand near the middle and others lie by Post's Lane. Post's Lane, a 20 foot lane, runs down the right side of the sheet, and the ends of the numbered streets of the adjoining sheets 105 and 106 meet it from the east: Eighth Street, Hudson Avenue, Seventh Street, Sixth Street, Fifth Street, Fourth Street, Third Street and Second Street. A compass rose is at the top. The margins name sheets 98 below, 101 and 105 and 106 at right.
notes: The subdivision streets (Bayley to Doane Avenues, 1st to 3rd Streets) were never built and have no modern equivalent; do not confuse them with the modern 1st to 10th Streets of the town centre.
Placed from three block corners carried from sheet 98, which is itself placed from sheet 104; the points lie along one line and scale and rotation come from the atlas, so confidence is low.
The right-hand streets are on sheets 105 and 106 and were not used for control.
Paper subdivision Bayley, Corrigan, Central (5th St), Doane Avs, 1st-3rd Sts; Post's Lane on the right; 100 ft.

sheet-98.description: Sheet 98 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north is toward the upper right. The upper left holds the lower part of a paper subdivision, a grid of 60 foot streets and uniform narrow lots that were laid out but not built: Halliard Avenue and Doyle Avenue run across the sheet and 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets run down it, with the blocks numbered 4 to 9 and 16 to 19. None of the blocks has any building. A diagonal line crosses the sheet from the left edge to the lower right and separates the subdivision from open marsh land to the south; Division Creek enters from the left edge. A few small dwellings and tar paper clad shacks marked vacant and dilapidated stand near the line. Post's Lane runs down the right side of the sheet; on its east side are the ends of Second Street, First Street, Minnie Place, Golden Avenue, Humboldt Place and Irving Place, which belong to sheets 103 and 104. A large open area between the subdivision and Post's Lane is divided by long lot lines. County Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet with Browns Lane leaving it to the north, and there is a small group of dwellings above County Avenue. The margins name sheets 97 above, 89 at left, 96 and 99 below and 101 at right.
notes: The numbered streets and Halliard and Doyle Avenues were never built and have no modern equivalent.
Placed from two block corners carried from sheet 104 (Humboldt Place and Irving Place at Post's Lane) with the atlas scale and a rotation from the lane; low confidence.
A third carried point (Golden Avenue) disagreed with the others by about 6 percent in scale and was not used.
Paper subdivision Halliard Av, Doyle Av, 1st-4th Sts; Post's Lane on the right, County Av at the bottom, Division Creek; 100 ft.

sheet-99.description: Sheet 99 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north is toward the upper right. County Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from the upper left margin to Paterson Plank Road at the upper right, with Brown's Lane running off it to the south east and down the sheet to rejoin the plank road near the bottom, enclosing a long wedge of land. The plank road runs down the right side of the sheet, drawn with its pipe line. Most of the buildings stand along County Avenue and the plank road. Along County Avenue to the right of Brown's Lane are dwellings and long greenhouse ranges with glass roofs, with more dwellings and sheds along the plank road. At the left margin on County Avenue are Public School No. 2, drawn in pink, and the Dutch Reformed Church. A row of narrow lots lies between Brown's Lane and the plank road at the lower right. The whole of the left and lower part of the sheet is open marsh land; Penhorn Creek winds across the lower middle and leaves the sheet at the bottom. A dotted line along the left side marks the edge of a lettered section of the atlas. Cedar Street is cut by the right edge at the top. The margins name sheets 98 and 101 above, 102 at right and 96 at left.
notes: Brown's Lane is taken to be today's Dorigo Lane by its spacing from the plank road; not confirmed.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions only (helmert fit), low confidence; the fitted scale is 3.4 percent below the nominal 100 ft value.
County Av, Brown's Lane, Paterson Plank Road, Penhorn Creek; 100 ft.

sheet-101.description: Sheet 101 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It is largely blank: the ground it shows is open farm land and lots divided by long property lines. Paterson Plank Road runs down the right edge. County Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet from the plank road at the right to the lower left corner, where Brown's Lane leaves it to the south. Post's Lane, a 20 foot lane, runs down the left side from the top toward the middle, and the lower end of Centre Avenue appears at the top where it is cut off by a property line near sheet 104. The few buildings are along the plank road. At the top is a small dwelling, then the Immaculate Conception Church with its heat, steam and electric lighting notation and a school building, a group of small dwellings and a glass greenhouse range in the middle, and Borough Hall, drawn in pink as a brick building with steam heat and electric lights, near the corner of County Avenue and the plank road. Several long diagonal lot lines cross the ground between Post's Lane and the plank road. A compass rose is placed at the upper left. The margins name sheet 104 above, 102 at right, 98 at left and 99 below.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Brown's Lane is taken to be today's Dorigo Lane by its spacing from the plank road (259 m drawn against 267 m modern); not confirmed.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions only (helmert fit), low confidence.
Post's Lane, Centre Av, Paterson Plank Road, County Av; Borough Hall, Immaculate Conception church; mostly blank; 50 ft.

sheet-102.description: Sheet 102 lies east of Paterson Plank Road, which runs down the left edge of the sheet, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north is toward the upper right. The sheet is mostly open ground. The built-up part is a strip along the plank road, where frame dwellings, shops and sheds stand on narrow lots and, at the upper left, the German Evangelical Lutheran St. Matheus Church lies beside the road. Cedar Street, a 20 foot street, leaves the plank road about a third of the way down and runs to the right to a road that runs down the sheet to meet a second road, which comes in from the lower left at the plank road. The block between these roads and the plank road holds a large range of greenhouses with glass roofs, a row of dwellings on deep lots, a wine shop, a hardware, oil and paint store, a saloon, storage sheds and a bowling alley at its lower end. A diagonal line crossing the right side of the sheet marks the edge of the farm land, and beyond it stand pig pens, sheds and a very large group of greenhouses in stepped ranges with a small dwelling and a boiler house at the lower right. Two long greenhouse ranges lie below the lower road. County Avenue joins the plank road from the west at the left edge just below Cedar Street. The margins name sheet 104 above, 101 and 99 at left and 99 below.
notes: Cedar Street is Cedar Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the road running down the sheet from it appears to be Cedar Lane.
Control points were hand-picked on the plank road, Cedar Street, the north-south road and the County Avenue stub; identities rest on spacing against modern nodes.
Fitted px_per_ft is about 2.8 percent above the atlas value for 50 ft sheets.
Paterson Plank Road, Cedar St, a road; greenhouses and a large works; 50 ft.

sheet-103.description: Sheet 103 shows part of the old centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned on the page so that Front Street runs across the top and north lies to the upper left. The part covers two rows of blocks between Front Street at the top and Post's Lane, which crosses the lower part of the sheet at a slight angle, with Centre Avenue running through the middle. The cross streets are, from left to right, 2nd Street, 1st Street, Minnie Place and Golden Avenue. The four blocks between Front Street and Centre Avenue are divided into narrow house lots, and many carry small frame dwellings, most of one and a half or two stories, with sheds and outbuildings behind them. A small shop for pearl buttons stands in the block between 2nd and 1st Streets near Front Street. The blocks south of Centre Avenue are more open and are dominated by greenhouses with glass roofs, in long ranges between 1st Street and Minnie Place and in a large group near Post's Lane at the left, reflecting the market gardening and flower growing for which Secaucus was known. Lots along Post's Lane are partly built, with a few dwellings and sheds. Water pipes are noted along Front Street and in the cross streets, and lot numbers are printed along every frontage. The margins name the adjoining sheets: 108 above Front Street, 106 to the left, 104 to the right and 98 below Post's Lane. The lower right of the sheet below Post's Lane is blank.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Post's Lane has no clear modern equivalent: it lies closer to Centre Avenue than today's Pandolfi Avenue or Raydol Avenue and was not used for control.
Greenhouses (glass roofs) fill much of the blocks south of Centre Avenue.
Town centre: Front St, Centre Av, Post's Lane, 2nd St, 1st St, Minnie Pl, Golden Av; greenhouses; 50 ft. Pilot. Pilot: 7 points, RMSE 1.03 m, ink 100.

sheet-104.description: Sheet 104 shows the east side of the old centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the grid turned so that north lies to the upper left. Paterson Plank Road crosses the top, running left to right and slightly downward; at the upper left it forks from Front Street, which runs off the left edge toward sheet 103, and the sheet carries the wedge of ground between the two roads. Centre Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, and Post's Lane, a 20 foot lane, runs along the bottom. Three streets cross Centre Avenue and run up to the plank road: Golden Avenue at the left, Humboldt Place in the middle and Irving Place to the right. The blocks along the plank road are the most built up. At the upper left a hotel with a saloon and bank office, a long bowling alley behind it, a drug store and a wagon shed stand on the corner of Front Street and Golden Avenue. Between Humboldt and Irving Places the frontage holds frame dwellings and stores, a club house and a post office building, with sheds behind. East of Irving Place there are storage buildings for furniture and for hay and feed. The deep lots running back from these buildings and the blocks below Centre Avenue are laid out in narrow lots, almost all of them empty except for a few dwellings, a workshop and sheds. A diagonal property line cuts across the right side below Centre Avenue. Water pipes of 5, 6 and 12 inches run along Front Street and the plank road. The margins name sheets 108 above, 103 at left, 101 and 102 at right and 98 below.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue, Humboldt Place is Humboldt Street, Irving Place is Irving Place and Golden Avenue is Golden Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Post's Lane has no modern equivalent along this line and was not used for control.
North arrow on the sheet points to the upper left; fitted rotation is about -38 degrees.
Paterson Plank Road / Front St, Centre Av, Post's Lane, Golden Av, Humboldt Pl, Irving Pl; 50 ft.

sheet-105.description: Sheet 105 shows two rows of blocks in the old centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned on the page so that Front Street runs across the top and Centre Avenue across the middle. The part lies between Front Street on the north east and Post's Lane on the south west, and between Hudson Avenue at the left and 5th Street at the right, with 6th and 7th Streets between them. The four blocks between Front Street and Centre Avenue are divided into narrow house lots, most of them carrying small frame dwellings and outbuildings, with a denser group of small buildings against Hudson Avenue. At the right-hand end of that row a fire department building with a hose wagon and ladder wagon stands on the corner of Front Street and 5th Street, and Public School No. 1, drawn in pink brick, stands on the block between Centre Avenue and 5th Street near the right edge. The blocks south of Centre Avenue are long, narrow lots running down to Post's Lane, which crosses the bottom of the sheet at a slight angle; they are sparsely built, with a scatter of dwellings, sheds and a few greenhouses. Water pipes are marked in the streets and lot numbers are printed along the frontages. The margins name the adjoining sheets: 109 above Front Street, 107 to the left, 106 to the right and 97 below Post's Lane. A compass rose stands in the right margin.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Hudson Avenue keeps its name.
Post's Lane has no clear modern equivalent here and was not used for control.
Public School No. 1 and a fire department building with hose and ladder wagons are drawn on the 5th Street end of the sheet.
Front St, Centre Av, Post's Lane, Hudson Av, 7th, 6th, 5th Sts; Public School No 1; 50 ft.

sheet-106.description: Sheet 106 continues the old centre of Secaucus to the east of sheet 105, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with Front Street across the top, Centre Avenue across the middle and Post's Lane crossing the bottom at a slight angle. The cross streets, from left to right, are 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets. The three blocks between Front Street and Centre Avenue are divided into narrow lots; a group of small buildings stands at the left against 5th Street, and the middle block carries a button works and a handful of dwellings, while the block between 3rd and 2nd Streets holds a few dwellings and a larger shed or barn. South of Centre Avenue the three blocks are almost entirely open lots, laid out in narrow parcels running down to Post's Lane, with only a few dwellings and one pink-coloured brick building near the top of the 5th Street block and a cluster of small buildings near Post's Lane at the lower middle. Water pipes are marked in the cross streets and Front Street, and lot numbers are printed on every frontage. The adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 110 above Front Street, 105 to the left, 103 to the right and 97 below Post's Lane. A compass rose stands in the lower right margin. The part overlaps the left edge of sheet 103, which begins at 2nd Street.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Post's Lane has no clear modern equivalent here and was not used for control.
The 3rd Street / Front Street junction was not detected.
Front St, Centre Av, Post's Lane, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd Sts; 50 ft.

sheet-107.description: Sheet 107 shows the western end of the old centre of Secaucus, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned on the page. Front Street runs along the top, Centre Avenue across the middle and Post's Lane across the bottom at a slight angle. From left to right the cross streets are 10th, 9th and 8th Streets, with Hudson Avenue at the right edge. The three blocks between Front Street and Centre Avenue are cut into narrow lots, most of them empty or holding a single frame dwelling, with a few small buildings along the frontages. South of Centre Avenue the three blocks are long lots running down to Post's Lane and are sparsely built; scattered dwellings and sheds stand near Centre Avenue and in the middle of the blocks, and a small building in light blue stands near the top of the block at Hudson Avenue. In the lower left corner a larger group of buildings stands on the corner of 10th Street and Post's Lane. Water pipes are marked in the streets and lot numbers are printed along every frontage. Margin notes name sheet 109 above, sheet 105 to the right and sheet 97 below. A compass rose stands at the upper left of the sheet. West of 10th Street the sheet is blank.
notes: Centre Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Hudson Avenue keeps its name.
Post's Lane has no clear modern equivalent here and was not used for control.
The building group at the lower left corner was read from the overview only and is not identified.
Front St, Centre Av, Post's Lane, 10th, 9th, 8th Sts, Hudson Av; 50 ft.

sheet-108.description: Sheet 108 lies north east of sheet 103 and is mostly open ground. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that Front Street runs down the left edge, with the town blocks of sheet 103 beyond it; only a 33 foot strip of Front Street and the ends of the cross streets that meet it are drawn. From top to bottom those cross streets are Third Street, Second Street, First Street, Minnie Place and Golden Avenue, each shown only as a stub with its name lettered in it. A dashed line near the top, lettered A, is a match line to a neighbouring sheet. Across the lower half of the sheet Paterson Plank Road runs from the lower left corner to the upper right as a wide diagonal road bordered by lots numbered in the 1300s on its north side; a pink brick building and a small green-tinted blacksmith shop stand beside it near the lower left, and a few frame buildings stand along Front Street opposite Second Street. The rest of the sheet is open meadow divided by property lines, with a few isolated sheds and a long narrow building at the right. Margin notes name sheets 110 above, 111 and 106 at the left and right of the top, 103 at the left, 104 at the lower left and 107 at the foot of the diagonal. A compass rose stands at the top.
notes: The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 103 and 105 to 107: Front Street runs down the left edge.

Placed on its Front Street junctions only (a helmert on points along one street), so confidence is low; the Front Street / Paterson Plank Road junction does not match the modern node and was not used.
Printed names Third, Second and First Street are 3rd, 2nd and 1st Street in OpenStreetMap; Minnie Place and Golden Avenue keep their names.
Front St (left), Paterson Plank Road; mostly blank; 50 ft.

sheet-109.description: Sheet 109 lies north east of sheets 105 and 107, across Front Street, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with Front Street along the bottom. Two rows of blocks run from Front Street up to Grace and are bounded at the left by 8th Street and at the right by 6th Street, with Hudson Avenue and 7th Street between them. The lower row, next to Front Street, is a row of long narrow lots with a mix of frame dwellings, sheds and some brick-coloured buildings in the 7th and 6th Street blocks. The upper row, between the street labelled Grace and the top of the platted blocks, is more sparsely built and has several rows of small dwellings in its middle blocks. Above the platted blocks the sheet is largely open ground, and the Public Service Railway Company's power house stands there, a large pink building with tracks, boilers, coal and engine rooms and a row of black circles for stacks or tanks, with smaller dots marking nearby poles. A pink building edge appears at the right margin, continuing on sheet 110. Water pipes are marked in the streets and lot numbers are printed on the frontages. Margins name sheet 107 and sheet 105 below, sheet 110 at the right and an adjoining sheet at the left and above. A compass rose stands at the top left.
notes: The street lettered Grace, 133 m from Front Street, was identified as modern Clarendon Street by its distance from Front Street; medium confidence.
Hudson Avenue keeps its name.
The 7th Street / Front Street junction was rejected as 11 m off the fit.
Public Service Railway power house; Grace St, Front St, 8th St, Hudson Av, 7th, 6th Sts; 50 ft.

sheet-110.description: Sheet 110 lies north east of sheets 106 and 105 beyond Front Street and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with Front Street along the bottom. Three long blocks lettered A, B and C run from Front Street up the sheet between 6th Street at the left, 5th Street and 4th Street, with a larger unplatted area to the right of 4th Street. A match line runs down the right side of the sheet. The blocks are divided into narrow lots and are almost empty; a few small frame buildings stand at the lower left near 6th Street and Front Street and a small cluster of buildings stands at the lower left of the 5th Street block. Grace Street is lettered at the left edge, where 6th Street meets it. The upper part of the sheet is open ground, on which stands the Public Service Railway Company's car house, a long pink brick building with its offices and storage tracks, and there is one small dwelling beside it. Third Street is lettered at the right of the lower margin. Water pipes are marked in the streets and lot numbers are printed on the frontages. Margin notes name sheets 111 above, 109 at the left, 108 at the right, and 105 and 106 below. A compass rose stands at the upper right.
notes: Grace Street, 132 m from Front Street, was identified as modern Clarendon Street by its distance from Front Street; medium confidence.
Placed on one detected point and three hand-picked modern junction nodes (modern node coordinates, pixels read on crops); low to medium confidence.
Third Street is printed in words; it is 3rd Street in OpenStreetMap.
Public Service Railway car house; Front St, Grace St, 6th, 5th, 4th Sts; 50 ft.

sheet-111.description: Sheet 111 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers a stretch of Paterson Plank Road in the north of Secaucus, running diagonally from the lower left corner towards the upper right. Maple, a 46 foot street, leaves the road at the middle of the sheet and runs up the page between two long blocks, marked A and B on the sheet, of narrow lots laid out for houses on both sides. Only a few of the lots are built on: a row of two-storey frame dwellings and sheds stands along both sides of Maple, a small group of dwellings faces the plank road below the east block, and a single Embroidery Factory with its own boiler heater, electric light and power plant, and steam heat stands on the west side of Maple, the only industrial building on the sheet. Water pipes are marked in the roadway, a 6 inch main in Maple and a 12 inch main in Paterson Plank Road, and dwelling numbers from 1433 to 1448 are printed along the plank road. In the upper left corner a large brick building with a lower extension stands alone in open ground, and below the plank road a few scattered dwellings and sheds stand in the lower left and lower right. The rest of the sheet is open marsh and meadow. The adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 110 to the left, 113 to the right, 115 below and 108 at the lower left; a dash-dot match line C to D crosses the lower left. A compass rose with the north arrow is in the upper left.
notes: Paterson Plank Road keeps its name in OpenStreetMap; the junction used here is Maple Street and Paterson Plank Road, about 40.79519, -74.05833.
Maple is Maple Street in OpenStreetMap, which runs north west from Paterson Plank Road at the same place.
Paterson Plank Road, Maple St; mostly blank; 50 ft.

sheet-112.description: Sheet 112 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the north end of Secaucus where Paterson Plank Road reaches the Hackensack River. The sheet is turned so that the plank road runs up the page from the lower left to the Hackensack Bridge at the top, and the river crosses the top of the sheet from left to right. Farm Road runs across the upper middle at right angles to the plank road, and below it a network of narrow lanes runs down the page: Hop's Lane along the left, Central Lane and Meadow Lane in the middle, and Stonewall Lane across the bottom, with Luhmann's Lane meeting it from below. Meadow Lane bends south east and ends at the lower right. The land between the lanes is a patchwork of farm and market garden lots, mostly open, with scattered dwellings, barns and sheds. A block of greenhouses fills the left middle, between Hop's Lane and Central Lane. Along the river bank on the right a long row of small frame buildings is lettered with the names of rod and gun clubs, boat clubs and similar societies, including Schammel Guards, Nautilus Boat Club, Palisade Rod and Gun Club, Lion Athletic Club, American L. S. Society, Oakdale Boat Club, Willow Boat Club, U. S. Vol. L. S. Corps, Lincoln Boat Club, Limit Boat Club and Meadow Boat Club. The remaining names at the lower end of the row are too small to read with confidence. A few buildings, one marked Hall, stand beside the plank road near the bridge. Water pipes are marked in the plank road. A compass rose is at the right edge.
notes: Hackensack Bridge is lettered on the plank road where it crosses the river; the modern road beyond it is outside this sheet.
Hop's Lane is Hops Lane in OpenStreetMap; Luhmann's Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Placed from three modern junctions only (Hops Lane with Paterson Plank Road, Farm Road with Meadow Lane, Central Lane with Stonewall Lane); the modern Hops Lane with Stonewall Lane node and Farm Road with Paterson Plank Road node lie about 15 m from their drawn positions and were left out.
The six boat club names at the lower end of the river row could not be read.
Paterson Plank Road at the Hackensack River bridge, Farm Road, Hops Lane, Central Lane, Meadow Lane, Stonewall Lane; 100 ft.

sheet-113.description: Sheet 113 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows Paterson Plank Road running from the lower left corner to the right edge, with two side streets joining it from opposite sides. Grace Av., 50 feet wide, runs up the page from the plank road along the middle of the sheet. Its east side is open and its west side is laid out as a long block of narrow lots, thirty or more, numbered along the street, of which only a handful near the plank road are built on, with pairs of frame dwellings and a barn. Fairview Av., a 20 foot street, leaves the plank road on the south side near the right and runs down the page towards sheet 115. East of Fairview, on the north side of the plank road, a large range of glass greenhouses lettered Green Houses, Storey and Glass Roofs, extends off the right edge into sheet 114, with an office at its west end. A dwelling and shed stand on a small lot west of Grace Av. beside the plank road. Away from the road the sheet is open land, with a few dwellings and sheds along the left edge and one building in the upper right corner. A 12 inch water pipe runs in the plank road. A compass rose is in the upper left. The neighbouring sheets are named in the margins: 111 to the left, 114 to the right and 115 below.
notes: Grace Av. is printed in abbreviated form; Grace Avenue is the OpenStreetMap name and runs north west from Paterson Plank Road at the same place.
Fairview Av. is Fairview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Placed on the Grace Avenue and Paterson Plank Road junction alone, at 7.5 px/ft with north from the neighbours; the Fairview Avenue junction measured 4.5 m from the anchored fit. Low confidence.
Paterson Plank Road, Grace Av, Fairview Av; greenhouses; 50 ft.

sheet-114.description: Sheet 114 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows Paterson Plank Road crossing the upper part of the sheet from the left edge to the top right, with Huber, a 38 foot street, leaving it on the south side and running down the page. The land on both sides of Huber is divided into narrow house lots; frame dwellings, some with stores or sheds, line both sides and numbers from 218 to 152 are printed along the street. On the west side of Huber, near the plank road, a row of lots backs on the plank road and holds sheds and small buildings; further down, Public School No. 3, a large brick building marked as heated by hot air and lit by electricity, stands on the west side, and behind it greenhouses, lettered Green Houses and Glass Roofs, continue from sheet 113 at the left edge. North of the plank road is a farm with a dwelling, sheds and chicken coops, and open pens partly covered with straw. Hop's Lane, 30 feet wide, runs down the right edge from the plank road to Stonewal Lane at the bottom right; between them lies open ground. A 6 inch water main follows Huber and a 12 inch main follows the plank road. A compass rose is at the top. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 112 to the right, 113 to the left and 116 below.
notes: Huber is Huber Street in OpenStreetMap; Hop's Lane is Hops Lane; Stonewal Lane is Stonewall Lane.

Placed by four points carried from sheet 112 along Hops Lane, which fix scale and rotation only along that lane; the fitted scale is about 8 percent below the usual 7.5 px/ft, so the lane is drawn shorter here than on sheet 112.
The modern Huber Street and Paterson Plank Road node lies about 10 m from where this sheet draws the junction and was left out.
The Stonewall Lane label is cut by the sheet edge after STONEWAL; the full name is printed on sheet 112.
Paterson Plank Road, Huber St, Hops Lane, Public School No 3; 50 ft.

sheet-115.description: Sheet 115 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers open farmland south of Paterson Plank Road, crossed from top to bottom by Fairview Av., a 20 foot street that continues from sheet 113. The land is divided by long east to west lot lines into large rectangular tracts, with the lines meeting a slanted boundary along the left edge and running on across Fairview to the right edge. Most of the buildings belong to a pig farm. The largest is a piggery with a boiling feed house, a water tank and an attached shed west of Fairview, with open wagon sheds, pig pens, a stable, a dwelling and several outbuildings lettered A to P scattered around it. East of Fairview a second group of farm buildings, lettered Q to V, includes dwellings, a long open shed and sheds. Along the left edge a short row of frame buildings and a few other sheds stand beside the slanted boundary, close to a compass rose in the upper left. No water pipes, house numbers or other streets appear. The adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 113 above, 111 to the left and 116 to the right. A black patch at the left edge near the bottom is a flaw in the scan or a tear in the paper.
notes: Fairview Av. is Fairview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

The sheet has no street junction; it is placed from three points carried from sheet 113, where the block line at the join meets the left boundary and the two edges of Fairview Av. The fitted scale is 7.47 px/ft.
Fairview Av; piggery; mostly blank; 50 ft.

sheet-116.description: Sheet 116 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers the south end of Huber, which comes down from sheet 114 at the top of the sheet. Huber is 38 feet wide with a 6 inch water main, and narrow house lots on both sides carry a few frame dwellings and sheds. Below the last lots Huber narrows to 20 feet and turns, becoming Huber Lane, which runs across the middle of the sheet to the right. At its right end Huber Lane turns again and runs down the page as a 15 foot lane to the bottom edge. A two storey building and a small dwelling stand at the corner where the lane turns. A second pig farm with a piggery, a boiling feed house, water tanks, pig pens and an open shed lies at the lower left, separated from the lanes by long east to west lot lines that continue from sheet 115. Most of the sheet is open meadow, bounded on the right by a long slanted line. A compass rose is at the upper right. The adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 114 above, 115 to the left, and no sheet is shown to the right or below. Dark tears in the scan cover part of the top margin, the lower right near the lane and the left edge near the bottom; none lies on a street.
notes: Huber is Huber Street in OpenStreetMap, but the modern street continues south east beyond the point where the drawn street turns into Huber Lane; Huber Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

No street junction exists on the sheet. It is placed on one point carried from sheet 114 (Huber east edge and a lot line, matched by lot count and checked against the lot lines of sheet 115), with scale 7.45 px/ft and north from the neighbours. Low confidence.
Huber St, Huber Lane; piggery; mostly blank; 50 ft. Small dark tears in the scan.
